latest_release.body:
**Download `exFAT.Image.Builder.exe`** below and run it: one file, nothing to install, no administrator rights. The first start unpacks the program once to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\kerrdec97\exFAT Image Builder\runtime` (with an empty `portable.txt` next to the exe: beside the exe instead).

Antivirus removes the exe? Download **`exFAT-Image-Builder-5.0.2-win64-folder.zip`** instead: the same program, already unpacked. Extract it anywhere and run the exe inside.

Check your download against `SHA256SUMS.txt`:
```powershell
Get-FileHash ".\exFAT.Image.Builder.exe" -Algorithm SHA256
```

## What's new in 5.0.2

Every part of the app was read line by line (engines, queue, launcher,
console code, every page, the build scripts and the tests); this version
carries the fixes, a design refresh and answers to the open GitHub issues.
Images built with 5.0.1 stay valid.

### From your reports (GitHub issues)
* **`ampr_emu.index` is back for exFAT and FFPKG builds** (#93). A game that
  uses the AMPR emulator (`fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx`) gets the index when the
  dump has none, and a fresh one when it no longer matches the game's files,
  as version 4 did. The index goes into the image only; the dump folder is
  never changed. New setting **AMPR file index** (Settings › Build, and under
  Advanced on the Build page): when the game uses the AMPR emulator
  (default), add when the dump has none, always rebuild, never add or change.
  PFS builds have the same new choice. The build log says what was done.
* **Add to queue makes a list** (#87). It puts the job on the list instead of
  starting it: add as many games as you like, then press **Start queue** (on
  the message, in the Jobs panel or on the Queue page). The main button
  ("Build image", "Pack game", …) still starts that one job at once. A waiting
  list is kept when the app is closed.
* **7z and RAR archives as build sources** (#37), as ZIPs already were:
  choose or drop `game.7z` or `game.rar`. For a multi-part RAR, choose the
  first part. Every file's checksum is checked while it is unpacked.
  Password-protected archives, solid RAR 4 archives and 7z archives using
  BZip2 are refused with a plain explanation.
* **Check dump** (#26): Library › Games › "Check dump…" reads a dump without
  changing it and lists missing or empty files, encrypted or cut-short
  executables, signs of a backport, junk files, links and names exFAT cannot
  store, with a report you can copy.
* **Where the app keeps its files** (#91, #90): Settings › Storage lists the
  unpacked program, settings, queue, logs and temporary files, each with
  "Show in folder". "Make this copy portable…" moves them next to the exe,
  for example on an external drive, copying your settings and queue; the
  switch happens at the next start.
* **Renaming images is easy to find** (#88): Library › Images has a "Rename
  images…" button, and a "Rename…" button when images are selected. Names can
  be "PPSA01234 - Title" or follow your own template, with a live preview.
* **Folder edition** (#78): each release also offers the program as a zip,
  already unpacked, for PCs whose antivirus removes the single exe.
* **Languages are back** (#35, #89): Settings › General › Language offers 42
  languages next to English: every language Windows 11 itself ships in, plus
  Persian, Urdu, Hindi, Bengali, Malay and Filipino. Arabic, Persian, Hebrew
  and Urdu mirror the whole window (right to left); paths, IDs and logs stay
  left to right. The interface switches after a restart ("Restart now"). Log
  files and error details from the engines stay in English. The translations
  are machine-made; "Show in folder" next to the setting opens a folder where
  you can correct a translation or add a language yourself (README.txt there
  says how).

# exFAT Image Builder 5 **Turn your PS5 game dumps into images that mount — and backport, convert, verify and send them to your console — from one app, in one download.** ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%20%2F%2011%20x64-3d7bff) ![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kerrdec97/ps5-exfat-builder?include_prereleases&color=8b5cf6) ![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/kerrdec97/ps5-exfat-builder/total?color=3d7bff) ![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-proprietary-8b5cf6) ![Home](docs/screenshots/home.png) > **Version 5 is a complete rewrite.** The app is now native C++/Qt: it > writes exFAT, UFS2 and PFS images itself, so it needs **no administrator > rights, no OSFMount, no .NET and no Python**, and it ships as **one .exe**. > > ⬇️ **Download 5.0.2** from the > [Releases page](https://github.com/kerrdec97/ps5-exfat-builder/releases): > one exe, nothing to install. > ⚠️ For games and content **you legally own and dumped yourself**. The app > does not download games, decrypt retail packages or bypass DRM, and it is > not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment. --- ## ✨ What it does | | | |---|---| | **Build image** | Drop a dump folder (or a zipped dump), pick a format, done. **exFAT**, **FFPKG** (UFS2), **PFS** (compressed `.ffpfsc` or plain `.ffpfs`), installable **FPKG** `.pkg` (with your own Sony Publishing Tools; from a folder, any image or a packed game), or a **Packed folder** (no image: the game folder with its files in zstd packs, for a USB drive or FTP). Each output shows only its own options; experts get the rest under *Advanced options*. **Performance mode** (Low impact / Balanced / Maximum) on every format. Every image is read back and verified before it gets its final name. | | **zstd packs** | *Compress game files*: the game's files go into zstd packs inside the image, served on the console by the bundled **ampr-emu-ng 0.3.3** runtime. Packed games (zstd or LZ4) are read through their packs everywhere: extract, convert, FPKG. Or skip the image: **Packed folder** packs the game folder itself. | | **Backport** | Make games run on older firmware with the built-in **PS5 Backport engine 0.3.4 by Deckerr97** — the same engine as the standalone PS5 Backport GUI, so results are identical. Target SDK 4–13, PS5 Pro fix, PS5 Pro build, AMPR / PlayGo switch, and optional apply to the game folder with a verified originals backup and one-click restore. | | **Backport updates** | Ship a backport as its own small **update package** that installs over the game's base package, so the base stays the original game: Build image › FPKG › **Backport** (4.xx and/or 5.xx+ backport files, folder or ZIP). Each update is checked against the base before it gets its name. | | **DLC** | Turn DLC lists (`dlc_emu.ini` and other DLC INIs) and DLC `.pkg` files into installable PS5 DLC packages, retarget them to another region's game, and save updated INIs (needs your own fpkg-cli). | | **Image tools** | Open an image to **extract** it (packed games come out as plain files; an image inside an .ffpfsc is read straight through), **verify** it (or compare it with a folder), **convert** between exFAT, FFPKG, FFPFSC and FFPFS, or **edit** it (add, replace, rename, delete files). | | **PS5 connect** | A real FTP file manager with a transfer queue, payload sender, kernel log and crash-dump capture, **ShadowMount+ 1.7** configuration (new format, safe-to-unplug), Fakelib manager, autoloader, AMPR index, Y2JB tools (firmware → YouTube version table, one-click install from your own YouTube packages) and package install. | | **Library** | Your dumps and images in a cover-art grid: formats at a glance, bulk build, backport, rename. | | **Queue** | Everything runs in a queue you can pause, reorder, cancel and retry while you keep working. The page you start a job from turns into its monitor: every stage with its time, a live progress bar, speed and time left, and the job's log as it is written. |

## ⚡ Quick start 1. Download **`exFAT Image Builder.exe`** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/kerrdec97/ps5-exfat-builder/releases) and check its SHA-256 (below). 2. Run it. The first start unpacks the app once (a second or two); later starts are instant. 3. **Build image** → drop your game folder (the one with `eboot.bin`) → pick a format → **Build image**. Portable use: put an empty `portable.txt` next to the exe and the app keeps its settings, logs and unpacked files in that folder. Antivirus removes the exe? Download the **folder edition** (`exFAT-Image-Builder--win64-folder.zip`) from the same release instead: extract it anywhere and run the exe inside. It is the same program, already unpacked, so nothing unpacks itself on first start. ## 🔐 Verify your download Every release from 5.0.0 has `SHA256SUMS.txt`. In PowerShell: ```powershell Get-FileHash ".\exFAT.Image.Builder.exe" -Algorithm SHA256 ``` The download arrives as `exFAT.Image.Builder.exe`: GitHub replaces the spaces in the file name with dots. Compare the hash with the line in `SHA256SUMS.txt`; capital and small letters make no difference. ## 🛡 Antivirus warnings The exe is not code-signed and it is a self-extracting program (it unpacks the app and the backport engine to your user folder on first start), which some antivirus engines flag by heuristics (`Wacatac`, `!ml`). These are guesses, not matches. You can check the hash or scan it on VirusTotal. ## 🧰 Requirements * Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11, 64-bit. * Optional: your own **Sony Publishing Tools** (`prospero-pub-cmd.exe`) for FPKG packages (backport updates need a verified SDK Fix release). Nothing from Sony is included or downloaded. * Optional: your own **fpkg-cli** (PSVIETHOA FPKG Builder, LibProsperoPkg by drakmor) for the DLC page. * For console features: a jailbroken PS5 running an FTP server (ftpsrv or etaHEN), and ShadowMount+ to mount images. ## 🙏 Credits Created and maintained by **Deckerr97** ([@kerrdec97](https://github.com/kerrdec97)).
